ethiopia.title: Ethiopia Secures Additional U.S.$8.5 Million in UN Humanitarian Funding
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia Secures Additional U.S.$8.5 Million in UN Humanitarian Funding - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia Secures Additional U.S.$8.5 Million in UN Humanitarian Funding 14 October 2026 The Reporter (Addis Ababa) By Beakal Teshome Ethiopia has secured an additional USD8.5 million in United Nations humanitarian funding to provide emergency assistance and protect civilians, with more than 202,700 people expected to benefit across regions facing acute humanitarian needs. Tom Fletcher, the UN under-secretary-general for humanitarian affairs and emergency relief coordinator, announced the allocation on October 13 through the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF). The funding will cover Tigray, Amhara, Afar and Benishangul-Gumuz, alongside other areas in need of urgent assistance. The allocation comes amid renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia that the UN has warned could deepen humanitarian needs and threaten regional stability. Secretary-General António Guterres expressed concern earlier this week over clashes in Tigray, Afar and Amhara, as well as reports of Eritrean forces in Ethiopia, warning of the risk of further escalation. The UN has also raised concerns about new displacement, civilian protection and disruptions to aid operations. The allocation will prioritise people affected by new or secondary displacement, communities facing disruptions to essential services and areas where humanitarian response capacity remains limited. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines From The Reporter Magazine Drought Emergency or Seasonal Deficit ? Published on 2026-09-02 By The Reporter Magazine What the Old Developmental State Got Wrong Published on 2026-10-02 By Samson Berhane 25-Year Sentences & Retroactive Laws: Controversial Draft Law Sparks Fears of Growing Authoritarianism in Tigray Published on 2026-06-21 By Yared Nigussie Red Sea Rivalries: What a Shifting Geopolitical Landscape Means for Ethiopia and The Horn Published on 2026-08-31 By Yared Nigussie The funds will support water, sanitation and hygiene, shelter, healthcare, nutrition and protection services, as well as shared services needed to facilitate humanitarian operations. "The additional resources will complement the significant response efforts already underway by the Government and humanitarian partners," said Ozonnia Ojielo, the UN resident and humanitarian coordinator in Ethiopia. The latest allocation brings CERF's total funding for Ethiopia in 2026 to more than USD22.5 million. The funding includes support for anticipatory action in Afar and Amhara, where El Niño-induced dry conditions have created additional humanitarian concerns. Read the original article on Reporter . ethiopia.title: IMF Postpones Ethiopia Review Schedule, Board Decision Slated for Early 2027
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: IMF Postpones Ethiopia Review Schedule, Board Decision Slated for Early 2027 - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: IMF Postpones Ethiopia Review Schedule, Board Decision Slated for Early 2027 14 October 2026 The Reporter (Addis Ababa) By Mintesinot Nigussie The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has scheduled discussions on Ethiopia's sixth review under its Extended Credit Facility (ECF) arrangement for November, with a final decision from the Fund's Executive Board expected in early 2027. The schedule pushes the process beyond the previously indicated October 15 milestone. An IMF spokesperson told The Reporter that November will mark the next round of talks on Ethiopia's reform programme. However, a formal decision on the sixth review will not occur until early 2027, when the assessment is presented to the Executive Board. The spokesperson did not disclose a firm timetable for either milestone. The IMF's fifth-review report, published in July, had previously noted October 15, 2026, as the earliest date for the next disbursement--projected at SDR 154.11 million, down from the originally planned SDR 191.70 million. The spokesperson emphasized that October 15 was merely the earliest window for potential fund distribution rather than a hard deadline for concluding the review, with actual fund releases remaining strictly contingent on Executive Board approval. The review process requires an IMF mission to travel to Ethiopia to evaluate economic performance and consult with government authorities. The mission then reports its findings to fund headquarters, where the Executive Board determines whether programme conditions have been met to allow subsequent disbursements. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn From The Reporter Magazine Drought Emergency or Seasonal Deficit ? Published on 2026-09-02 By The Reporter Magazine What the Old Developmental State Got Wrong Published on 2026-10-02 By Samson Berhane 25-Year Sentences & Retroactive Laws: Controversial Draft Law Sparks Fears of Growing Authoritarianism in Tigray Published on 2026-06-21 By Yared Nigussie Red Sea Rivalries: What a Shifting Geopolitical Landscape Means for Ethiopia and The Horn Published on 2026-08-31 By Yared Nigussie In a separate exchange with The Reporter , Julie Kozack, the IMF's Director of Communications, noted that the Fund could not yet pin down a completion date, as the mission must first meet with Ethiopian authorities before presenting its assessment to the board. "What will happen before we conclude the next review is we have a mission, and a team will go to Ethiopia and talk with the authorities. They will come back and present the report to the Executive Board," Kozack said. The fifth review, completed on July 1, disbursed approximately USD 464 million and brought cumulative disbursements under the four-year, USD 3.4 billion programme to about USD 2.647 billion. The IMF reported that Ethiopia met all quantitative performance criteria for end-December 2025 and achieved most indicative targets, alongside notable progress in exports, foreign-exchange reserves, and government revenue. From The Reporter Magazine From Unwilling Investors to Bidding Wars: Ethiopia's T-Bill Market Turns on Its Head Published on 2026-09-03 By Mahlet Mehdi Washington Has Sent a Sufficient Signal to PM Abiy on Military Operations: Ex-CIA Analyst Published on 2026-09-28 By Bewket Abebe Behind Ethiopia's Stalled Iron Ore Mining Published on 2026-08-29 By Bewket Abebe Cities as Engines of Growth and Nation-Building: Reframing Urbanization Discourses in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) Published on 2026-09-14 By Mussie Delelegn Arega (PhD) Those results, however, cover an earlier assessment period and do not dictate the outcome of the sixth review, which evaluates Ethiopia's performance against targets set for the end of June 2026. Approved in July 2024, the ECF arrangement supports Ethiopia's broader economic reform agenda, which aims to correct macroeconomic imbalances, strengthen public finances, and foster private-sector-led growth. Since entering the programme, the government has introduced income tax modifications, stepped up tax compliance and customs administration, liberalized the foreign-exchange market, and gradually reduced fuel subsidies to raise domestic revenue and relieve public finance pressures. These measures have coincided with a sharp rise in tax collection. Federal tax revenue surged by 76 percent in the first nine months of the 2025/26 fiscal year compared to the same period a year earlier, driven by adjustments to income and fuel taxes, according to IMF data. General-government tax revenue is estimated to have climbed from 6.2 percent of GDP in 2023/24 to 9.5 percent in 2025/26. During a fiscal policy press briefing on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok on Wednesday, The Reporter asked Davide Furceri, a division chief in the IMF's Fiscal Affairs Department, whether aggressive tax hikes and subsidy cuts are appropriate for Ethiopia given its massive informal sector and structural productivity constraints. Furceri responded that nations starting from a very low tax-to-GDP base, such as Ethiopia and Nigeria, must mobilize additional domestic revenue to fund essential public spending and service debt. "For many countries that are starting from a very low tax rate base, like Ethiopia and Nigeria, it is important to raise sufficient revenue," Furceri said. Beyond expanding the tax base, Furceri stressed that governments must eliminate structural distortions in their tax systems that hamper economic activity. Addressing these inefficiencies can improve revenue collection without imposing undue burdens on the economy. He also cautioned against dismissing targeted subsidies simply because a country lacks comprehensive national registries or digital payment systems. While building such infrastructure remains a crucial medium-term priority, governments can deploy alternative strategies immediately. "Countries need to prepare for this in the medium term. In the short term, there are alternatives, including school-feeding programmes and geographically targeted support," he said. Read the original article on Reporter . ethiopia.title: Somaliland, Ethiopia Discuss Defence Cooperation, Regional Development
ethiopia.content: Somalia: Somaliland, Ethiopia Discuss Defence Cooperation, Regional Development - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Somalia: Somaliland, Ethiopia Discuss Defence Cooperation, Regional Development 14 October 2026 Horn Diplomat (Hargeisa) By Mohamed Duale Hargeisa — Somaliland's army chief has met Ethiopian diplomatic and defence officials to discuss strengthening military cooperation and addressing regional security concerns, according to a statement posted on the Somaliland National Army's official social media account. Brigadier General Nimcaan Yuusuf Gaaxnuug held the meeting at the army's headquarters in Hargeisa with Ethiopian envoy Teshome, Ethiopia's consul general in Somaliland and the embassy's defence attaché. The talks focused on defence relations between Somaliland and Ethiopia, strengthening security cooperation and addressing security challenges in the region, the statement said. Teshome briefed Gaaxnuug on recent developments in the region during the meeting. The army chief reaffirmed Somaliland's commitment to closer cooperation between the two militaries to support regional peace and stability, according to the statement. ethiopia.title: Emergency Aid Reaches Climate-Affected Communities in Afar
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: Emergency Aid Reaches Climate-Affected Communities in Afar - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: Emergency Aid Reaches Climate-Affected Communities in Afar 14 October 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Emergency humanitarian assistance is reaching drought-affected communities in Afar Region, Ethiopia, targeting vulnerable households and people in need following climate-induced challenges. The first round of relief supplies, dispatched from the central grain warehouse in Adama city, is being delivered to high-priority individuals and families across the region. In Girifo Kebele of Bidu Woreda, residents have begun receiving the assistance, which beneficiaries say has arrived at a critical time as drought continues to strain their livelihoods and access to food. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Meyrem Abdu, one of the beneficiaries, said the assistance would help support her children and other family members who have been facing food shortages. She expressed appreciation for the government's response to the situation affecting communities in the region. Asiya Mohammed, another beneficiary, said the intervention would help ease the hardship facing her family and other residents. He further noted that the support was particularly important given their difficult circumstances. On his part, Team Leader of Inventory Quality and Control at the Afar Region Disaster Risk Management Commission, Mohammed Abdella said the distribution was targeting the most vulnerable groups in affected areas. He explained that the region had previously been mobilizing its own resources to support drought-affected communities and was now supplementing those efforts with additional relief supplies dispatched by the Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission. Bidu Woreda Agriculture and Natural Resources Office Head, Yesuf Mohammed said drought associated with climate change had caused significant hardship for local residents, describing the humanitarian intervention as timely and essential. The ongoing distribution is intended to provide immediate relief to affected households as authorities mobilize assistance for communities facing the impacts of drought. The humanitarian supply comes amid ongoing efforts by regional and federal authorities to support drought-affected communities and address food shortages in vulnerable areas, as ENA learned. ethiopia.title: Ethiopia Calls for Faster, Better-Coordinated Sovereign Debt Restructuring
ethiopia.content: East Africa: Ethiopia Calls for Faster, Better-Coordinated Sovereign Debt Restructuring - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français East Africa: Ethiopia Calls for Faster, Better-Coordinated Sovereign Debt Restructuring 14 October 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Ethiopia has called for a more streamlined and predictable sovereign debt restructuring process, urging stronger creditor coordination and enhanced cooperation under the Common Framework to help countries restore financial stability and unlock development financing. Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE), Eyob Tekalign made the call while addressing the Global Sovereign Debt Roundtable (GSDR) on the sidelines of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. Drawing on Ethiopia's debt restructuring experience, Eyob stressed the need for clear timelines for countries entering the process, improved coordination among creditors, and early caps on advisory fees to make restructuring more efficient and predictable. Looking ahead, Ethiopia urged the GSDR to prioritize deeper cooperation among Bretton Woods institutions, reconsider rigid eligibility criteria for countries emerging from restructuring whose credit ratings remain temporarily impaired, and improve coordination of new financing to support national development priorities, it was indicated. ethiopia.title: Ethiopia Shifts Focus From Debt Relief to Investment At Global Summit
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia Shifts Focus From Debt Relief to Investment At Global Summit - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia Shifts Focus From Debt Relief to Investment At Global Summit 14 October 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Ethiopia is strengthening its international financial partnerships while shifting its focus from debt restructuring to attracting fresh investment capital, Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia, Eyob Tekalign underscored. Approached by The Pulse of Africa from Bangkok, where he is leading an Ethiopian delegation to 2026 International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group Annual Meetings, Eyob said the country's international economic engagement is increasingly guided by national priorities. He noted that the summit offers Ethiopia a vital platform to deepen economic partnerships, attract foreign investment, and secure development financing on its own terms. The country aims to secure high-value partnerships that reflect its historical standing, market size, and broader economic potential. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines The strategy builds directly on major breakthroughs in external debt relief. Ethiopia has fully finalized agreements with bilateral creditors and is rapidly concluding negotiation terms with commercial lenders, having already reached an agreement in principle with Eurobond holders. With its debt profile restored, Ethiopia is using the global gathering to pursue additional development financing and showcase its economic reform model. The Governor noted that Ethiopia is actively sharing its practical restructuring experiences with other developing nations navigating similar fiscal challenges. Addressing global partners, Eyob emphasized that Ethiopia's international engagement remains firmly grounded in its national priorities rooted in Medemer philosophy. He said Medemer (synergy) draws on Ethiopian roots and provides a pragmatic foundation for the country's development path. "Medemer is something that is excavated from Ethiopian roots, while the starting point is always Ethiopians. We don't have any other ideology except Ethiopia itself, in a very pragmatic approach to development," he said. Domestically, the central bank is driving a historic opening of the banking sector to foreign competition after five decades of tight restrictions. The policy aims to inject fresh capital, spur dynamic competition, and introduce modern financial services across the country. Rather than weakening local institutions, the reform encourages domestic banks to boost their capital reserves and operational resilience. ethiopia.title: Ndakimana Tips Rwanda to Overturn Ethiopia Deficit in LA 2028 Qualifiers
ethiopia.content: East Africa: Ndakimana Tips Rwanda to Overturn Ethiopia Deficit in LA 2028 Qualifiers - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français East Africa: Ndakimana Tips Rwanda to Overturn Ethiopia Deficit in LA 2028 Qualifiers 12 October 2026 The New Times (Kigali) By Peter Kamasa Tuesday, October 13 Olympic Qualifiers (Second Leg) Ethiopia vs Rwanda (Dire Dawa Stadium, Ethiopia) Rwanda women's national team captain Angeline Ndakimana is confident that Amavubi can overturn their first-leg deficit and eliminate Ethiopia when the two sides meet in the return leg of the 2028 CAF Women's Olympic Qualifiers at Dire Dawa Stadium on Tuesday. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Rwanda head into the decisive encounter trailing 1-0 on aggregate following a heartbreaking defeat in the first leg in Kigali on October 7. Despite the setback, Ndakimana believes Amavubi have the quality and determination to respond away from home and keep their Olympic qualification hopes alive. "We made a mistake in the first leg, but we can turn things around away from home. They are a good team, but we can beat them," Ndakimana said. "We have been preparing well for this match because we know how difficult it is going to be. Everyone in the team is focused on achieving a positive result," she added. Head coach André Casa Mbungo shares his captain's optimism, insisting that the team has worked to address the shortcomings that cost them in the first leg. "We corrected our mistakes and we want to make sure that we get a good result. I know it is hard, but it is possible," Casa Mbungo said. The first leg appeared destined to end in a goalless draw before a stoppage-time own goal by Rwanda defender Lydia Uzayisenga handed Ethiopia a crucial advantage. Uzayisenga inadvertently turned Abebe Mihiret's cross into her own net in the second minute of added time, leaving Rwanda with a difficult task ahead of the return fixture. With their Olympic dream on the line, Amavubi must produce a strong performance in Ethiopia to keep their qualification campaign alive. Rwanda need to win by at least two goals to overturn the deficit and secure progression to the third round. The winner of the tie will advance to the next stage, where either Tanzania or Botswana awaits as the qualification campaign continues. Read the original article on New Times .
